title: Headless Chromium sends localhost through the proxy and times out silently
appliesTo: Any environment where HTTP_PROXY or HTTPS_PROXY is set, including most agent sandboxes and many corporate CI runners.
claim: A headless browser launched in an environment with proxy environment variables set routes even http://localhost requests through that proxy, so navigation to a local dev server hangs until the navigation timeout with no error naming the proxy.
expectation: Loopback traffic bypasses an HTTP proxy, so a browser reaching a dev server on localhost behaves the same as curl does.
reality: Chromium honours the proxy for loopback addresses unless told otherwise. The failure is a bare navigation timeout naming only the URL and the wait condition. Because curl to the same URL succeeds — curl applies its own no-proxy defaults — the natural conclusion is that the server is slow, the wait condition is wrong, or the page never settles. Time goes into tuning waitUntil and raising timeouts, none of which can work.
mechanism: Proxy configuration and loopback exclusion are separate settings. Chromium applies the configured proxy to all schemes it is given and does not infer a bypass for localhost, while most CLI HTTP clients exclude loopback by default. The tools disagree, and only one of them says so.
workaround: Launch with `--proxy-server=direct://` and `--proxy-bypass-list=*` for local-only runs, or set an explicit bypass list including localhost and 127.0.0.1. When a navigation to a local server times out while curl to the same URL returns 200, suspect the proxy before touching the wait condition.

evidence.note: The server was plainly up and fast.

evidence.output:
page.goto: Timeout 30000ms exceeded.
Call log:
  - navigating to "http://localhost:3200/", waiting until "networkidle"
evidence.note: No mention of a proxy. The log points at the wait condition, which is the wrong place to look.
Ten full-page screenshots captured immediately after, with no other change to the server or the page.

check.command: Start any local HTTP server, confirm curl reaches it, then navigate a headless browser to the same URL with HTTPS_PROXY set, first without and then with --proxy-server=direct://
check.confirmedIf: navigation times out with proxy env vars set and succeeds once the proxy is bypassed, with no other change
check.refutedIf: navigation succeeds with the proxy configured, meaning loopback is excluded by default

observations.note: Cost the most time of anything in this session's screenshot work. I first suspected the wait condition and changed networkidle to load, which did not help; the proxy bypass did, immediately.

environment.note: Claude Code remote sandbox, Linux 6.18.44, HTTPS_PROXY set
